name: recall-persistent-memory
description: Persistent, searchable developer memory that Copilot uses autonomously. Hybrid keyword + semantic search, automatic file indexing (30+ languages), passive event capture, deduplication, import/export, and a bundled offline AI model. 100% local and private.

chatParticipants.name: recall
chatParticipants.description: Search, save, and manage persistent developer memory

languageModelTools.name: recall_search
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search persistent developer memory for observations, bug fixes, and insights
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the developer's persistent memory for recorded bug fixes, architectural insights, and prior investigations. Use when: the user reports a bug, error, or unexpected behavior; you are about to modify or refactor a function; you need to understand how a module or API works; you are planning a feature that touches existing code. QUERY STRATEGY: Use a two-tier approach. TIER 1 (context-first, run when entering a new subsystem): broad architectural queries using only the module name, e.g. {"query": "auth architecture"} or {"query": "payments dataflow"}. Memory stores what was LEARNED, not what you are GUESSING — symptom-only queries usually miss prior context. TIER 2 (symptom, run after Tier 1): function + module + symptom, e.g. {"query": "getAccessToken refresh race condition", "tags": "auth,bugfix"}. RETRY ON 0 RESULTS: do not conclude 'no prior knowledge exists' from a single miss. Retry at least 2-3 times with broader queries, different tags, or the parent module name before proceeding without recall context. Returns: a ranked list of observations, each with id, trust status (✓verified = confirmed fact, ⏳pending = unverified), age, source, project label, tags, and the full observation text. Current-project results appear first; cross-project results appear after, labeled [from: ProjectName]. Do NOT use this for looking up file structure or symbol names — use recall_file_index for that. Do NOT skip this before editing code; a prior fix may already exist.

query.description: 2-6 keywords: function name + module + symptom or concept. Example: 'getAccessToken refresh race condition'. Do not pass the full user message as the query.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags to filter results. Example: 'auth,bugfix'. Omit to search all tags.

limit.description: Max results to return. Default: 10. Increase to 20 for broad investigations.

project.description: Override auto-detected project name. Omit to use the current workspace folder name.

languageModelTools.name: recall_save
languageModelTools.userDescription: Save a new observation to persistent developer memory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Save an observation to persistent memory THE MOMENT you learn something durable — NEVER batch saves at the end. Call this tool incrementally at each milestone: after mapping how a subsystem works; after confirming or disproving a hypothesis; after discovering a cross-file dependency; after identifying a bug root cause. A typical investigation MUST produce 2-5 observations, not one summary at the end. CRITICAL RULES: (1) ONE CLAIM PER OBSERVATION ALWAYS — if [WHAT] has more than one sentence, you MUST split into separate saves. Multi-sentence observations dilute the semantic embedding and become unfindable by search. (2) ALWAYS split architecture from bugfix — learning how something works AND finding a bug in it = TWO separate saves, not one. (3) Save DURING investigation not after — save the architecture observation the moment you understand the system, BEFORE finding the bug. FORMAT: Use the 'kind' field and structured content: '[WHAT] single-sentence claim. [WHERE] file, function, line. [WHY] reason this matters.' EXAMPLES by kind: (architecture) {"content": "[WHAT] AuthService refreshes tokens through a shared singleton; all callers await the same promise. [WHERE] src/auth/authService.ts refreshToken() L89. [WHY] Any caller that bypasses this creates a duplicate refresh race.", "kind": "architecture", "tags": "auth,architecture"}. (gotcha) {"content": "[WHAT] The payments webhook handler must be idempotent — Stripe sends duplicates. [WHERE] src/payments/webhook.ts handleEvent() L34. [WHY] Without dedup, charges double on retry.", "kind": "gotcha", "tags": "payments,gotcha"}. (dataflow) {"content": "[WHAT] User permissions flow: JWT claims → middleware → req.user → route guard. [WHERE] src/middleware/auth.ts → src/guards/role.ts. [WHY] Adding a new role requires changes in both files.", "kind": "dataflow", "tags": "auth,dataflow"}. (bugfix) {"content": "[WHAT] Race condition: concurrent getAccessToken() calls all pass expiry check before any refresh completes. [WHERE] authService.ts getAccessToken() L142. [WHY] Fix: added mutex around refresh block.", "kind": "bugfix", "tags": "auth,bugfix,concurrency"}. Returns: confirmation with observation ID. Saved as 'pending' until the engineer verifies. Do NOT save: trivial facts the file index already captures; build/git results (passive capture handles those); unconfirmed guesses; vague summaries like 'fixed auth bug'.

content.description: Structured observation. Use format: '[WHAT] one-line claim. [WHERE] file, function, line. [WHY] reason this matters for future work.' Be specific enough that a future session can find and act on this without reading the file.

kind.description: Category of observation. architecture = how components connect; bugfix = root cause + fix; gotcha = non-obvious trap; dataflow = how data moves across files; contract = API/interface constraint; hypothesis = confirmed or disproved theory; decision = design choice and rationale.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags: module name + category. Example: 'auth,bugfix,concurrency'. Categories: bugfix, architecture, gotcha, dataflow, performance, config, concurrency.

languageModelTools.name: recall_file_index
languageModelTools.userDescription: Look up cached file structure — function names, line numbers, descriptions
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Look up the cached structural summary of a source file before reading it. Use when: you are about to call read_file on any source file; you need to find which line a specific function starts on; you want to know what functions/classes a file contains without reading it; you know a symbol name but not which file it is in (use symbolQuery). Example: {"query": "authService.ts"} or {"query": "src/", "symbolQuery": "getAccessToken"}. Returns: one-sentence file description, list of all function/class/struct symbols with exact line numbers and brief descriptions, total line count. Use the returned line numbers to read only the specific function you need instead of the whole file — this saves 1,000-8,000 tokens per file. If the file is not indexed, the result will be empty; read the file normally and it will be indexed on next save. Do NOT use this for searching bug fixes or prior knowledge — use recall_search for that.

query.description: File path or filename. Can be absolute, workspace-relative, or just the filename. Example: 'authService.ts' or 'src/services/authService.ts'.

symbolQuery.description: Search for a function/class/symbol name across all indexed files. Use when you know the symbol name but not which file contains it. Example: 'getAccessToken'.

languageModelTools.name: recall_ask
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask the developer a clarifying question with selectable options instead of guessing
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask the developer a clarifying question and get an immediate, authoritative answer instead of guessing about the codebase. Use this the MOMENT you are uncertain about intent, scope, an architectural decision, a convention, a requirement, or which of several valid approaches to take — BEFORE you start investigating or assuming. This prevents wasted tokens spent reading files to infer something the developer can confirm in one click. Provide 2-5 concrete, mutually-exclusive options whenever possible; an 'Other (type a custom answer)' choice is added automatically so the developer can type a free-form answer. The returned answer is GROUND TRUTH — do not re-question it; proceed immediately. Set reusable=true when the answer is durable knowledge that will matter in future sessions (architectural intent, a convention, a design decision, a non-obvious requirement) so it is saved as a verified memory; set reusable=false for one-off, task-local answers (e.g. 'which file should I edit right now'). If the developer dismisses the prompt, you will be told to proceed with your best judgment. Do NOT use this to ask trivial questions you can answer yourself by searching memory (recall_search) or the file index (recall_file_index) first. Example: {"question": "Should the new cache be in-memory or persisted to disk?", "options": ["In-memory (lost on reload)", "Persisted to disk"], "reusable": true, "tags": "cache,architecture"}.

question.description: The clarifying question to ask the developer. Be specific and concise. Example: 'Should the new cache be in-memory or persisted to disk?'

options.description: 2-5 concrete, mutually-exclusive answer choices shown as a picker. An 'Other (type a custom answer)' entry is appended automatically unless allowCustom is false. Omit to ask a free-form (text input) question.

allowCustom.description: Whether to append an 'Other (type a custom answer)' option to the picker. Default: true.

reusable.description: Set true if the answer is durable knowledge worth saving for future sessions (architectural intent, conventions, design decisions). Set false for one-off, task-local answers. Default: false.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags used only when reusable=true. Example: 'cache,architecture'.

recall.databasePath.description: Custom path for the Recall database. Leave empty to use the default (~/.recall/recall.db).

recall.autoIndexOnSave.description: Automatically index file symbols when a file is saved.

recall.pendingExpirationDays.description: Number of days before unverified pending observations are automatically expired.

recall.idlePromptMinutes.description: Minutes of inactivity before prompting to save session notes. Set to 0 to disable.

recall.maxSearchResults.description: Maximum number of search results returned by recall_search.

recall.projectName.description: Project name for tagging observations. Defaults to the workspace folder name if empty.

recall.indexFileExtensions.description: Additional file extensions to index (e.g. [".vue", ".svelte"]). Common languages are indexed by default.
